newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks sink over 100 points as bonds slide.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks sink over 100 points as bonds slide.

text.p: Wall Street stocks sank over 100 points shortly after the market open on Friday, hurt by steep declines in bond prices which revived lurking market concerns about the possibility of higher rates.

In early trade, the Dow Jones Industrial shed 101 points, or 1.23 percent, at 8086, prompting the New York Stock Exchange to set curbs on index-arbitrage trading six minutes after the open. It set sidecar curbs at 0915 EDT/1315 GMT.
The long bond, which started a downward spiral on Thursday after the U.S. Treasury released results of a $10 billion auction of 30-year bonds, lost 20/32 to yield 6.57 percent.
Deteriorating technical factors, market supply, a lower dollar and a strong cyclical outlook were cited as reasons behind the bond market's slump on Friday.
The Nasdaq composite lost 17 points to 1606.

"Bonds are coming to grips with a stronger possibility of a new economic scenerio," Pierre Ellis, senior economist at Primark Decision Economics, said. "Plus, the dollar is very unstable, which is a disincentive for foreigners to be here."
